summary: Monumental Mountain summit lookout, Stevens County: 60-ft pole tower 1945, DNR 40-ft tower 1965, removed 1996; top 10 feet rebuilt on private land.

facts.design: 40-foot DNR timber tower with live-in cab (1965), preceded by a 60-foot pole tower with a 6-by-6-foot cab and cabin (1945)
facts.status_note: Tower removed from the summit in 1996; its top 10 feet were rebuilt on private land by Rod Fosback

staffing.status: Staffed from 1945; last staffed in 1980 per the Former Fire Lookout Sites record, until the mid-1980s per the National Historic Lookout Register

facts.agency: Washington Department of Natural Resources (1965 tower)

events.note: 60-foot pole tower with a 6-by-6-foot cab and a cabin
Dan Reeder of Rice employed as lookout at the summit cabin
Washington DNR replaced the pole tower with a 40-foot timber tower and live-in cab; Forest Lookouts gives 1964-66
Last staffed in 1980 per the Sites record; Lookout Register says staffed until the mid-1980s
Removed from the summit to make room for another radio tower
Sold to FFLA member Rod Fosback, who moved it to his own woodland; Forest Lookouts says sold and moved to private property
firelookout.com says Fosback rescued the tower and placed it on his hillside property in 1998

evidence.supports: 60-foot pole tower with cab and cabin built 1945; 40-foot DNR timber tower built 1965; last staffed 1980
evidence.quote: Preceded by a 60' pole tower with 6'x6' cab and cabin built in 1945, this 40' timber tower with DNR live-in cab, built in 1965, was last staffed in 1980.

evidence.supports: removed from the summit in 1996 to make room for another radio tower
evidence.quote: The tower was removed in 1996 to make room for the addition of another radio tower on the summit.

evidence.supports: Fosback rebuilt the top 10 feet with its cab on his land east of Colville
evidence.quote: The lookout was purchased and rescued by Rod Fosback who has rebuilt the top 10' of the tower with cab on his land east of Colville.

evidence.supports: site is in Stevens County, Washington
summit is eight miles southwest of Colville
Viola Frahm listed as lookout in 1957; Margo Moulder in 1980
evidence.quote: Known lookout personnel: 1957: Viola Frahm; 1958: Loretta Young; 1960: John Dodson; 1979: Lee Ellen Philpott; 1979 relief: Margo Moulder; 1980: Margo Moulder; 1980 relief: Lee Ellen Philpott.

evidence.supports: state forestry office reported the road construction complete on August 11, 1945
evidence.quote: August 11, 1945: Completion of initial construction of the road leading to Monumental lookout is reported by the local office of the state division of forestry.

evidence.supports: observation cabin set up at the summit with Dan Reeder of Rice as lookout
evidence.quote: An observation cabin has been set up at the summit, with Dan Reeder of Rice employed as lookout.

evidence.supports: a state report dates the tower erection to 1964-66
evidence.quote: 1964-66: A lookout tower erected. (5th Biennial Report of the Washington Department of Natural Resources)

evidence.supports: sold and moved to private property in 1996
evidence.quote: 1996: Sold and moved to private property.

evidence.supports: built by Washington DNR in 1965, replacing a 1945 state tower
evidence.quote: It was originally built by the Washington Dept. of Natural Resources on Monumental Mountain near Colville in 1965, replacing a state tower dating to 1945.

evidence.supports: staffed until the mid-1980s, then declared surplus
evidence.quote: Staffed until the mid 1980s, the lookout was declared surplus.

evidence.supports: sold in 1996 to Rod Fosback, who moved it to his own woodland; cab is 14 by 14 feet with a catwalk on a 10-foot wood tower
evidence.quote: The 14' x 14' flattop DNR cab with catwalk on a 10' wood tower was sold in 1996 to FFLA member Rod Fosback who carefully moved it to his own woodland.

evidence.supports: surviving tower is on private land overlooking the Little Pend Oreille River
evidence.quote: Fosback Lookout is located on private land overlooking the Little Pend Oreille River in northwestern Washington.

evidence.supports: FFLA is the Forest Fire Lookout Association
Fosback placed the tower on his hillside property in 1998
evidence.quote: was rescued by Rod Fosback and placed on his hillside property in 1998.

corrections.proposed: Washington Department of Natural Resources (built the 1965 tower)
corrections.why: The Sites record's Administered-by line names the owner of the removed tower, not the lookout's operator; the Lookout Register says the Washington DNR built the lookout.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The Sites record and the Lookout Register give 1965; the Forest Lookouts page quotes a state report giving 1964-66.
The Sites record says last staffed in 1980; the Lookout Register says staffed until the mid-1980s.
The Lookout Register gives 1996 for the sale and move; firelookout.com gives 1998 for placing it on Fosback's hillside. No source explains the gap.
The Sites record gives the 1965 tower as 40 feet; the Lookout Register describes the surviving 10-foot wood tower. The 40-foot figure is used for the site, the 10 feet for the surviving part.

notes_for_editor: This record covers the summit site. The surviving tower is already covered by us-wa-monumental-mountain-lookout-site-at-fosback, which cites several of the same sources, so check for overlap. No fetched source describes the summit today, so access is omitted; the brief's 'unknown' stands. The Sites record also links a separate Monumental Mountain Lookout Site (Colville NF, US 1515), which is not covered here. The Lookout Register has a 1996 photo of the tower at its original site (courtesy Rod Fosback); no image URL appeared in the fetched text, so no photo was added. The 1965 vs 1964-66 and 1996 vs 1998 dates are both reported as conflicts in the story.
